cards.headline: Fundraising Target Nearly Reached: When to Amend?
body: Example: KRW 100M target, KRW 92M raised, KRW 20M expected next week.
cards.promise: When to apply and what to prepare
cards.takeaway: Check amendment registration before the original fundraising target is reached.
cards.design: Use the even-numbered episode's calendar illustration and three decision paths; emphasize the KRW 8M gap.

cards.headline: Only KRW 8M Left—but KRW 20M Expected

body.text: Registered fundraising target on the certificate.
Corporate donation due next week, not yet received.

cards.takeaway: If the donation arrives, the original target will be exceeded by KRW 12M.
cards.design: Use proportional bars for registered, collected and scheduled amounts, highlighting the conditional excess.

cards.headline: When Must You Apply to Increase the Target?

body.text: Apply before the registered period ends and before the original target is reached.
Apply at least two weeks early, the portal advises; this is not a statutory 14-day rule.
Submitting a request does not mean the increased target is already registered.

cards.takeaway: File before the target is reached and confirm completed registration.
cards.design: A calendar shows the window before the original target, with clearly separate filing and completion stages.

cards.headline: Which Stage Is Your Nonprofit In?

body.text: Prepare the increased target and revised use plan before the original limit is close.
Reconcile receipts and scheduled donor payments, then confirm the procedure with the registry.
Stop fundraising immediately; check the completion report due within 30 days after stopping.

cards.takeaway: What you do next depends on whether the target has already been reached.
cards.design: Three decision columns distinguish time remaining, nearly reached, and already reached.

cards.headline: First, check whether the target has been reached.
cards.takeaway: Identify your stage before the next step.
cards.design: Spacious mid-series rest card with one prominent conclusion and three paths.

cards.headline: Bank Balance Is Not Total Donations Collected

body.text: Compare KRW 92M received with the registered target, not today's bank balance.
After KRW 30M in spending, KRW 62M could remain, but KRW 92M was collected.
KRW 20M expected next week is not yet part of actual receipts.

cards.takeaway: Track what was collected, what remains, and what is only expected.
cards.design: Compare cumulative receipts, remaining balance, and future donations as distinct figures.

cards.headline: Four Steps Before Filing an Amendment
body: Check the registration certificate for the target, period, and purpose.
Reconcile total receipts with scheduled donor payment dates.
Record why more funding is needed and revise the use plan.
Attach revised fundraising and use plans to the amendment form.
cards.takeaway: Align the certificate, receipts, revised plans, and application before filing.
cards.design: Four numbered document steps, from original certificate to updated application.

cards.headline: Raising the Target Is Not Changing the Purpose

body.text: If the existing project expands, explain why additional funding is needed and provide an updated use plan.
If donations will fund a different project, check whether a change of purpose or separate registration must be considered.

cards.takeaway: Raising the amount and changing what donations will fund are separate decisions.
cards.design: Contrast additional funding for the same purpose against funds for a different project.

cards.headline: Match Your Website to the Updated Registration
body: After registration is amended, update the target and period on the donation page.
Check social posts and corporate donor notices for outdated targets and dates.
While the amendment is pending, do not present the higher target as registered.
cards.takeaway: Do your published target and period match the current registration?
cards.design: Check the registered certificate against the website and donor-facing communications.

cards.headline: Before New Donations, Prepare These Records

body.text: Gather the existing registration certificate, cumulative donation records, and the amount and expected date of the additional contribution.
Compare the current target and period with planned changes, and identify what the revised fundraising and use plans need to address.

cards.takeaway: A free preliminary review can clarify amendment needs and which documents to prepare.
cards.design: Show the three source records and the two or three concrete first-review outcomes in separate columns.
